dedupe_keys.name: free5gc open source 5g core network linux foundation project

description: free5GC is an open-source implementation of the 5G core network (5GC) defined by 3GPP, hosted as a Linux Foundation project. Its README states the goal of implementing the 5GC of 3GPP Release 15 and beyond, and the project site now speaks of Release 17 and beyond, with a service-based architecture of separate network functions. Coverage: generic software, not tied to a network or country. The latest release named on the site is v4.2.3, which added a redesigned web console and a free-ran-ue chart for Kubernetes deployments. Format and access: Go source code on GitHub, a user guide, tutorials and a free self-paced Linux Foundation course (LFS114); free. Licence: Apache 2.0, read from the repository licence file. Caveats: this is the core network only; a radio access network or a simulated one is needed to attach devices, and the software was not built or run for this record. Simulation uses: building mobile network testbeds and digital twins in which core network functions can be failed, overloaded or attacked to study service resilience and capacity. Related records: UERANSIM (platform-ueransim) simulates the user equipment and gNodeB that such a core serves, and Open5GS (platform-open5gs-open-source-5g-lte-core) is an alternative core.
